_note: Performance/scale tier (W1-23), reported separately from the correctness boards (board S0). Inputs come from scale_inputs.py (generated_files, sha256-checked). timeout_seconds = max(20, 10 x the reference's time when the suite was written, scale.timing); scale.natural_program is the plausible program each task stresses and scale.observed its class and time on each binary. Never merge into another suite.

tasks.title: Ten million generator steps
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that runs the generator `x = (1103515245 * x + 12345) % 2147483648` for 10000000 steps starting from x = 1, adding `x % 7` to a running total after each step. Print `x = <final x>` and `total = <total>`. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: raw VM cost per loop iteration (10^7 steps); the Python reference gives the comparison
scale.fix: none planned -- the baseline the other tasks are read against

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Sort 5000 generated Ints
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that generates 5000 Ints with the generator `x = (1103515245 * x + 12345) % 2147483648`, starting from x = 42 and stepping once before each value; value k (k = 0..4999) is `x % 100000` after the k+1-th step. Sort the 5000 values ascending. Print `first = <v0> <v1> <v2> <v3> <v4>` (the five smallest, ascending, single spaces), `last = <v4995> <v4996> <v4997> <v4998> <v4999>`, `median = <(v2499 + v2500) / 2 with integer division>` and `checksum = <sum over k of k * v_k, modulo 1000000007>`. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: quadratic insertion sort (the guide's template) on 5000 elements in the VM's per-op cost; P2 on a `sorted(xs)` helper

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: 10,000 binary searches over 100,000 sorted Ints
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program that builds a sorted `Int[]` `a` of 100000 elements with `a[i] = 3 * i + 1` for i = 0..99999, then answers 10000 membership queries with binary search: query j (j = 0..9999) looks for `q = (j * 7919) % 300007`. Print `found = <number of queries whose value is in a>` and then `index sum = <sum, over the found queries, of the index where q sits in a>`. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: P2: an array parameter is copied eagerly on every call, so a `bsearch(xs: Int[], target: Int)` helper called 10^4 times copies 10^9 elements

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Memoised recursive Fibonacci
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program with a memoised recursive Fibonacci (fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1, fib(n) = fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)): each value is computed once and remembered. Print `fib(30) = <v>`, `fib(60) = <v>` and `fib(90) = <v>` on three lines (fib(90) = 2880067194370816120 fits Aether's 64-bit Int). Then print `sum = <fib(0) + fib(1) + ... + fib(90)>`. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: P2 and array value semantics: a memo `Int[]` parameter is copied into each call, so the callee's writes never reach the caller and the recursion is exponential
scale.fix: W-runtime P2 copy-on-write / by-reference arrays (D8, open)

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Depth-first search over a 1000-node graph
tasks.prompt: Write an Aether program for a directed graph with nodes 0..999 where node u has edges, in this order, to `(u * 7 + 3) % 1000`, `(u * 13 + 11) % 1000` and `(u + 1) % 1000`. Run a depth-first search from node 0 that visits neighbours in that edge order and marks a node visited when it is first reached (pre-order). Print `reachable = <number of visited nodes>`, `first = <the first 8 nodes in visit order, single spaces>` and `checksum = <sum over visit positions p (0-based) of p * node, modulo 1000000007>`. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: P2: a recursive dfs(u, adj: Int[][], visited: Bool[]) copies the adjacency table and the visited array on every call (10^3 calls x 4x10^3 elements)

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Scan a 100 KB text character by character
tasks.prompt: A text file named `corpus.txt` (about 100 KB) is in the working directory: lines of lowercase ASCII words separated by single spaces, each line ending with a newline. Write an Aether program that reads the whole file into a single Text (its lines joined with newline characters) and then scans that Text character by character to compute: the number of characters that are letters, the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u), the number of words (maximal runs of letters), and the length of the longest word. Print `letters = <n>`, `vowels = <n>`, `words = <n>` and `longest = <n>`, one per line. Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: P3: Text indexing `s[i]` is O(i), so a character scan of a 100 KB Text is quadratic

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Word frequencies over 20,000 words
tasks.prompt: A text file named `words.txt` is in the working directory: 20000 lowercase words drawn from about 2000 distinct ones, ten per line, separated by single spaces. Write an Aether program that counts how often each distinct word occurs. Print `words = <total words>` and `distinct = <number of distinct words>`, then the 10 most frequent words as `<rank>. <word> <count>` (rank 1 to 10; higher counts first, ties broken by the word in alphabetical order). Print nothing else.

scale.stresses: no map type: the parallel-array lookup the guide teaches is a linear scan per word (20000 x ~1700 Text compares)
scale.fix: a Tally/map idiom or builtin (open); VM speed

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))

tasks.title: Roll up a 5 MB JSON order file by region
tasks.prompt: A JSON file named `orders.json` (about 5 MB) is in the working directory, shaped `{"orders": [{"id": Int, "region": Text, "sku": Text, "qty": Int, "cents": Int}, ...]}` with 65000 orders. Regions are `central`, `east`, `north`, `south` and `west`. Write an Aether program that parses the file and, for each region in that alphabetical order, prints `<region>: orders=<count> qty=<sum of qty> revenue=<sum of qty * cents, as dollars with exactly two decimals>`. Then print `orders = <total count>` and `largest = <id of the order with the largest qty * cents; the lowest id on a tie>`. Close the document. Print nothing else.
tasks.expected_stdout:
central: orders=13054 qty=65532 revenue=32952542.22
east: orders=12900 qty=64845 revenue=32569152.20
north: orders=13115 qty=66173 revenue=33403470.26
south: orders=12937 qty=64646 revenue=32536086.73
west: orders=12994 qty=64969 revenue=32769348.18
orders = 65000
largest = 4772

scale.stresses: P4: toon_at(arr, i) walks the array from the start, so iterating 65000 orders is quadratic; there is no linear form today

timing.rule: timeout_seconds = max(20, ceil(10 x the slower reference time))
